lessons.title: Telling the Time

items.exampleMeaning: It's one o'clock in the afternoon.

items.example: A che ora inizia il film?
items.exampleMeaning: At what time does the movie start?

lessons.tip: In Italian, when telling time, use 'è' for one o'clock and 'sono' for all other hours. Remember to use the definite article before the hour, like 'le' for plural hours.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: A che ora inizia il treno?
dialogue.meaning: At what time does the train start?

scenario.partnerRole: A is a friend asking about the time and train schedule.
scenario.learnerRole: B is the learner providing the time and information.
scenario.brief: You are discussing the time and train schedule with your friend. Answer their questions about the time and when to meet.
scenario.goal: You need to tell the time and answer questions about meeting.

lessons.title: Buying Tickets

items.exampleMeaning: I would like a ticket to Rome.

items.example: Quanto costa un biglietto per Milano?
items.exampleMeaning: How much is a ticket to Milan?

items.example: Ecco il mio biglietto per il treno.
items.exampleMeaning: Here is my ticket for the train.
Where can I buy a ticket?

items.meaning: At what time does it leave?
items.example: A che ora parte il bus?
items.exampleMeaning: At what time does the bus leave?
I'll take a ticket to Florence.

lessons.tip: When buying tickets, you can ask 'Quanto costa un biglietto?' to know the price. Use 'un biglietto per...' to specify your destination.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Where can I buy a ticket?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Puoi comprare un biglietto alla stazione.
dialogue.meaning: You can buy a ticket at the station.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Quanto costa un biglietto per Roma?
dialogue.meaning: How much is a ticket to Rome?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: A che ora parte il treno?
dialogue.meaning: At what time does the train leave?

scenario.partnerRole: A is a ticket seller at the station.
scenario.learnerRole: B is the learner buying a ticket.
scenario.brief: You are at the station asking about tickets. Make sure to ask about the price and the departure time.
scenario.goal: You need to buy a ticket and know the departure time.

lessons.title: Using Verbs in Present Tense
lessons.tip: The present tense in Italian is formed by changing the verb endings. For example, 'andare' (to go) becomes 'vado' (I go) for the first person.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Are you waiting for the train?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I wait for the train.

scenario.partnerRole: A is a friend asking about your plans.
scenario.learnerRole: B is the learner explaining their transport plans.
scenario.brief: You are discussing your travel plans with a friend. Use present tense verbs to describe what you do.
scenario.goal: You need to explain where you go and what you take.

lessons.title: Combining It All

items.example: Posso avere un biglietto per Firenze?
items.exampleMeaning: Can I have a ticket to Florence?

items.meaning: At what time do we meet?
items.example: A che ora ci incontriamo alla stazione?
items.exampleMeaning: At what time do we meet at the station?

items.example: Arriviamo in tempo per il treno?
items.exampleMeaning: Do we arrive on time for the train?

lessons.tip: Use 'quando' to ask about time and 'dove' to ask about places. These questions help you gather information about your plans.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: We are going to the restaurant.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Posso avere un biglietto per Roma?
dialogue.meaning: Can I have a ticket to Rome?

scenario.partnerRole: A is a friend planning a trip together.
scenario.learnerRole: B is the learner discussing the trip details.
scenario.brief: You and your friend are planning a trip. Ask questions and provide information about the time and tickets.
scenario.goal: You need to clarify the trip details and make plans.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Quanto costa un biglietto per Roma?
dialogue.meaning: How much is a ticket to Rome?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Arriviamo in tempo per il treno?
dialogue.meaning: Do we arrive on time for the train?

scenario.partnerRole: A is a friend discussing plans.
scenario.learnerRole: B is the learner confirming details.
scenario.brief: You and your friend are reviewing your plans for the trip. Discuss the time, tickets, and where you are going.
scenario.goal: You need to confirm your travel plans.
